subject: PO requirements and invoice cadence constraints for upcoming renewal
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@mediance.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@mediance.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: PO requirements for Redwood renewal - invoice cadence and discount caps

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed. Before we move to signature, procurement needs to confirm a few constraints so our AP systems can accept Redwood invoices. Can you review and let me know if you can comply or provide alternatives?

Key constraints from our side:
- Single PO per legal entity per month (we cannot accept multiple invoices against the same PO within that month unless line items are milestone-tagged).
- We require EDI 810 or PDF invoice with PO number in the header for automated matching.
- Standard net45 payment terms for vendors without early-pay programs.
- Discounts >10% require pre-authorization from Sourcing and need to be spread across billing periods rather than applied as an upfront credit.
- Invoice cutoff for month-end processing is the 25th (invoices dated after the 25th are processed in the following month).

Attached is our PO template and our Accounts Payable contact. Please confirm: can Redwood issue a consolidated month-end invoice per entity with PO reference and an itemized line for usage + overage? If you have suggested approaches (split invoices, milestone tagging, or early-payment discounts), share them and any impact on pricing.

Best,
Asha Patel
Director, Procurement
Mediance Health
procurement@mediance.com

Attachment: Mediance_PO_Template.pdf (application/pdf)

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@mediance.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO requirements for Redwood renewal - invoice cadence and discount caps

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear note and the template. Short answers up front: yes to PO reference, yes to itemized consolidated invoices; EDI 810 we support via our billing partner (will need setup). A few clarifying points and options we recommend: 

1) Single PO per entity / month: We can produce a consolidated monthly invoice per legal entity that references a single PO number. If your team needs internal line-item splits (e.g., product vs. overage vs. support), we can provide those as separate line items on the same invoice.

2) EDI 810 / automated matching: Our billing ops uses a middleware provider that can send EDI 810. We will need procurement team to share EDI endpoint + qualifiers. As a fall back, we can produce a PDF invoice that follows your PO header format.

3) Net45 terms: Our standard commercial program is net30, but for enterprise accounts we can accommodate net45. That will impact the unit pricing slightly. For a net45 commitment we can preserve the proposed discount tiers but with slightly reduced volume-based credits (I can pull numbers once you confirm expected monthly spend).

4) Discounts >10%: We can structure discounts to be applied as an invoice-level credit that is amortized across monthly invoices rather than a one-time lump sum. If Sourcing requires the discount to be staged, we can include a discount line with an agreed allocation schedule (e.g., prorated across 12 invoices).

5) Invoice cutoff: We can accept a 25th cutoff and run billing on the 26th with a month-end consolidated PDF/EDI file. Any usage that posts after your cutoff will appear on the following month’s invoice. 

Next steps I propose:
- We provide a short one-page billing ops checklist for your AP team (EDI fields, PO header mapping, remittance info).
- Vanessa (cc’d) will coordinate the middleware/EDI setup and provide the contact at our billing partner.
- Kar (cc’d) will create a pricing delta scenario showing (a) net30 standard, (b) net45 with preserved discount tiers, and (c) net45 with staged discount amortization.

If that sounds good, I’ll loop in Finance and Legal to document the finalized billing cadence in the SOW/contract language.

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Credit_App.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@mediance.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@mediance.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO requirements for Redwood renewal - invoice cadence and discount caps

Hi Grace — this is helpful, thanks. A couple follow-ups from Sourcing/AP: 

- We can proceed with EDI 810; our endpoint details are attached in the template. Can your billing partner support ISA/GS qualifiers for our ERP (Coupa)?
- Sourcing prefers discounting applied as a monthly amortized credit for our budget forecasting. The request is specifically that any discount over 10% be applied pro rata month-to-month.
- For net45: Sourcing will accept net45 if Redwood confirms there will be no change to the invoicing frequency (still one consolidated invoice per month) and that any staged discount schedule is reflected as credits on each invoice.

If you can provide the pricing delta scenarios and the one-page EDI checklist by end of week, Procurement will prepare the PO and route for signature. Also include the legal billing clause wording we should expect (a short redline).

Regards,
Asha

Action items: 
- Vanessa: please reach out to our billing partner and confirm ISA/GS support for Coupa; get turnaround estimate for EDI onboarding and any integration cost. Capture contact and timeline.
- Kar: please run the pricing delta scenarios that show the impact of shifting from net30 to net45 across the three tiers in the current SOW; show one column with amortized discount vs one-time credit. Target: provide a short spreadsheet by Friday EOD so I can send to Asha and Sourcing.
- I will draft the billing clause language for Legal that explicitly states the amortization schedule and PO mapping expectations.

Notes for negotiation: we should preserve list price but make a commercial concession in payment terms rather than additional % discount. If they push for >15% effective discount we should require Sourcing approval and get it documented.

Thanks — Grace
